text:
alana: quick design review note from hallway test: permalink semantics are confusing when we canonicalize routes. Two concrete issues: 1) hash fragments (/#/models/12345) vs pathname permalinks behave differently re: left-nav reveal and focus restoration; 2) breadcrumb shows alias name then flips to canonical name after redirect which looks like a flash of wrong context.

jess: can you give a short repro?

alana: repro: open an external permalink to /models/alias-foo#revisions -> page loads, body gets focus, URL quickly rewrites to /models/12345 (canonical) and breadcrumb shows "Models > 12345" for a moment then "Models > alias-foo" when alias resolves. Nav stays collapsed.

mike: summary: router rewrite + alias resolution order causes breadcrumb flicker and nav not reconciled. Also hash vs pathname change means history entries differ which breaks back button expectations.

sara: accessibility callouts: when we programmatically update the URL we should also update aria-current and avoid moving focus away unexpectedly. For hash-fragment anchors we must ensure skip links and "Go to main" still work.

tom: proposals (short):
 1) canonicalize URL before render and reconcile nav state synchronously in router restore hook. This avoids breadcrumb flicker.
 2) for hash-fragment permalinks, normalize to pathname+fragment server-side and treat as external navigation so we reveal nav.
 3) add a small keyboard quick-jump ("g n" or "/ n") that reveals left nav and focuses search input without changing history.

jess: UX tradeoffs: pre-canonicalize helps reduce flash but means user sees canonical path immediately which might be surprising if alias is friendlier. Maybe show alias in UI but canonical in address bar? Need PM input.

leah: product note: alias vs id visibility matters for support docs and copy. We prefer stable canonical URLs for reproducibility but friendly aliases are OK in UI. Could add an optional "copy friendly permalink" action that returns alias form.

mike: implementation detail: router emits two events: before-resolve (we can fetch alias mapping) and restored. If we fetch mapping in before-resolve we can rewrite location via history.replaceState so no extra stack entry, then mount with final path and call reconcileNav(path). Use preventScroll:true when focusing.

sara: a11y specifics: when we reveal nav due to external permalink, set aria-live polite: "Navigation: Models  alias-foo revealed". Ensure focusable element has tabindex=0 and role=link, and expose a visible focus ring. Also test with VoiceOver and NVDA.

jess: breadcrumb copy suggestion: show alias visually with a secondary hint (muted) showing canonical id: "alias-foo  · id:12345" so users see both and we avoid flash. On hover expand to full context.

tom: analytics: track event nav.reveal.source = {external, internal, quickjump} and breadcrumb.flash boolean for telemetry. This will help us decide whether to auto-reveal.

mike: test plan: unit for history.replaceState use, e2e for back/forward with permalinks and hash fragments, accessibility e2e for live region & focus ring, keyboard quick-jump unit + e2e.

leah: product ok with canonical-first approach if we expose friendly alias in UI and provide copy-friendly permalink action.

alana: action items: (1) eng (mike) implement canonicalize-before-mount + reconcileNav in router.beforeResolve; (2) a11y (sara) add live region + test matrix; (3) design (jess) mock breadcrumb dual-label pattern and quick-jump microcopy; (4) product (leah) add copy-permalink action to backlog. I'll open issue #4987 and PR with feature-flag gating.

design-bot: Figma note added: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/breadcrumb-permalinks (comment by @jess).

alana: thanks all 44d if no objections I'll file the PR and tag eng-router for edgecases.
